scenario.briefing: A rover console reads a port from a maintenance file. Bad text and out-of-range numbers must be distinguishable.

accessibility.summary: The Zig workspace is keyboard accessible. Checks verify source structure; they do not compile or run Zig.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between the editor and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, whether it passed, and the missing or forbidden source fragment.

title: Error unions at the input boundary
summary: Return typed errors from a port parser, then diagnose a catch that reports every failure as out of range.

objectives.description: Return typed errors from a parser.
Separate a parse failure from a range failure.
Predict how catch handles a parser error.

hints: An error set names each failure the function can return.
Use catch return to map a parse failure to InvalidNumber.
Check the range before casting down to u16.

misconceptions.description: Discarding a parse error with catch unreachable.
misconceptions.testDescription: Parse failures return InvalidNumber and the range is checked.
misconceptions.feedback: Bad input is not unreachable. Return a typed error or handle the failure explicitly so a malformed file cannot crash the rover console.

misconceptions.description: Turning every parse failure into zero.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Using catch 0 so malformed port text becomes a valid-looking zero.
misconceptions.feedback: A silent zero erases the difference between bad syntax and a real value. Preserve the error in the return type.

misconceptions.description: Reporting a parse failure as OutOfRange.
misconceptions.feedback: Parsing text and checking a numeric range are different failures. Keep the parse error separate so the console can explain the input problem.

misconceptions.description: Expecting catch to propagate the error unchanged.
misconceptions.feedback: catch handles the error at that expression. Use try when the caller should receive it.

sections.title: Error sets name failure
sections.body: A function can return an error union: PortError!u16, where PortError is an error set such as error{ InvalidNumber, OutOfRange }. The caller must handle both possibilities. Zig errors are values, not exceptions, and the compiler checks that every error is handled or propagated with try.

sections.title: try and catch choose a boundary
sections.body: try returns the error to the caller and unwraps the success value. catch handles it on the spot: value = parseInt(...) catch return PortError.InvalidNumber. catch unreachable asserts that failure cannot happen and panics in safe builds if it does, so reserve it for states the type system proves impossible.

sections.title: Validate before narrowing
sections.body: std.fmt.parseInt(u32, text, 10) can represent values above a port's range. Parse into the wider type, reject zero and values above 65535, then use @intCast(value) in the u16 return context. Casting first can overflow before the range check.

vocabulary.definition: A named collection of errors a function can return.
A return type that carries either a value or an error.
An expression that unwraps a success or returns the error to the caller.
An expression that handles an error union at the current boundary.

steps.title: Parse a rover port
steps.prompt: Edit main.zig. parsePort returns InvalidNumber for malformed text and OutOfRange when the number is zero or above 65535.
hints: Keep the PortError set and the !u16 return type.
Parse into u32 so large values can be checked.
Map a parseInt failure to InvalidNumber with catch return.
Reject zero and values above 65535 before the cast.

steps.title: Every bad port looks out of range
steps.prompt: The console reports OutOfRange even when the text is not a number. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.
hints: The parse failure happens before any range check.
catch currently maps every parseInt error to OutOfRange.
Return InvalidNumber from the parse failure.
Keep the range check for parsed numbers separately.

instructions.label: const value = std.fmt.parseInt(u32, text, 10) catch return PortError.OutOfRange;

fixes.label: Return InvalidNumber from the parse failure, then check the range separately.
Parse directly as u16 so overflow cannot happen.
Use catch unreachable for malformed text.

steps.explanation: The catch maps every parseInt error to OutOfRange, so the console cannot tell bad text from a large number. Parse as u32, map parse failures to InvalidNumber, and check the range on the value.

steps.title: Catch at the call site
steps.prompt: A caller writes `const port = parsePort(text) catch 8080;`. What happens when text is not a number?
hints: catch handles the error union at this expression.
The fallback value becomes the expression result.

quiz.prompt: A caller writes `const port = parsePort(text) catch 8080;`. What happens when text is not a number?

options.label: The error is handled here and port becomes 8080.
The error propagates to the caller of this function.
The program panics in every build mode.
The code does not compile because catch needs try.

quiz.explanation: catch consumes the error at that expression and substitutes the fallback. Use try instead when the caller should receive the error.
